newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee association sees sizeable price rise.
newsitem.headline: German coffee association sees sizeable price rise.

text.p: Germany's coffee industry association DKV said "significant" retail price rises were inevitable to compensate roasters for rising costs.
A DKV statement on Monday said world market arabica prices had risen to $245 from $165 per 60-kg bag over the last two months.
German roasters had incurred additional costs in procuring dollar-denominated green coffee because the dollar had risen to 1.68 marks from 1.45 in the same period.
The industry's sales in 1996 amounted to 8.1 billion marks, down by one billion from 1995, the statement also said. Within the total, instant coffee sales accounted for 1.1 billion marks.
The decline in sales was the result of falling revenue from lower retail prices which had averaged 7.01 marks per 0.5 kilos of roasted coffee compared with 7.98 marks in 1995.
Sales volumes of roasted and instant coffee in 1996 were only slightly down by 0.4 percent, at 562,250 tonnes, green coffee basis, and equivalent to 9.4 million 60-kg bags.
Per-capita consumption in Germany, the world's second largest coffee consumer, was steady at 6.9 kilos.
Roasted coffee sales accounted for 527,200 tonnes green coffee basis (529,500 in 1995).
